findings.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed WITHOUT underline)
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining was added to CHARACTERS in the BLOCK CONTAINS clause of the Relative I-O FD general format. In the printed diagram CHARACTERS is an optional word (not underlined), so 'BLOCK CONTAINS 512' with neither word is legal; the markdown makes CHARACTERS a key word, i.e. one of the two words must be written, which is falsely restrictive.

findings.markdown_says: # 4.4 THE OPEN STATEMENT ... ## 4.4.1 Function ... ## 4.4.2 General Format ... ## 4.4.3 Syntax Rules ... ## 4.4.4 General Rules
findings.why_it_matters: Headings at the wrong level: the sibling sections 4.2 CLOSE and 4.3 DELETE (pages 447, 449) are '##' with '###' subsections, but 4.4 is promoted to a level-1 heading and its 4.4.x subsections to level 2, so a heading-based index puts OPEN at chapter level, outside section 4.

findings.pdf_says: A file may be opened with the INPUT, OUTPUT, EXTEND, and I-O phrases in the same run unit. ... preceded by the execution of a CLOSE statement, without the LOCK phrase, for that file. (EXTEND, and 'without the LOCK phrase,' are boxed, with no square brackets)
findings.markdown_says: (5) A file may be opened with the INPUT, OUTPUT, [║EXTEND,║] and I-O phrases in the same run unit. ... a CLOSE statement, [║without the LOCK phrase,║] for that file.
findings.why_it_matters: Square brackets not printed in the standard were added around the boxed (high-subset) text; elsewhere the transcription marks boxed text with ║...║ alone, and the brackets read as an optionality notation the rule does not carry.
